## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd50ef25315a838988c2086cd5f2d6733bbc7b08`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-field-key-grammar-refused.ts + packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`objectExtensions: z.array(ObjectExtensionSchema)`, the `defineStack` and `os validate` door), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extension-item.ts (`OBJECT_EXTENSION_ITEM_SCHEMA`, the save, restore, promotion and sync door), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`registerStoredObjectExtension`, the boot and heal hydrations), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts (the `__c` judge the changeset's "Unchanged" line names), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`registerApp`'s `objectExtensions` fold), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (the install's extension reads), packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts (`object_extension` to `objectExtensions`), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-field-patch-key-grammar-refused.ts (the sibling entry), packages/spec/src/shared/record-proto-key-guard.ts, .changeset/29523-object-extension-field-key-grammar.md (read for ②, not reviewed)

Inputs: card #29523 (body, triage 6584774842, claim 6593404228, os-dev-report 6595183097), PR #29774 (body, 8-file list, net diff of `bd50ef25` against merge-base `87956dcc` of `main`), and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, `ObjectExtensionSchema.fields`: the record key moves from `z.string()` to `FieldNameKeySchema` (`/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/`), the one constant `ObjectSchema.fields` (object.zod.ts:3212) and `ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldPatches` (object.zod.ts:5081) already read. Narrowing, correctly judged: `Region Code`, `RegionCode`, `region-code`, `2nd_phone`, `Region Code__c` are refused; `region_code` and `region_code__c` still parse. The `fields` key set is now exactly the key set the target's own map admits, which is the card's "done when". Right.
- Issue shape: one `invalid_key` at `fields.KEY` through the record's `error` map, the same mechanism and path convention as the `fieldPatches` reader (#29366). The message names the grammar, two examples and no tracker number (`check:doc-authoring` holds). `__proto__` stays refused on the raw input by `refuseRecordProtoKey`, unchanged; `constructor` and `prototype` stay admitted on the extension (as on `fieldPatches`, noted on #29513 and again in the report's out-of-scope list), so the agreement test rightly leaves them out. Right.
- Public surface: no export added or removed; `FieldNameKeySchema` stays unexported; the `fields` `describe` changes, which is the one `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` row the regeneration moved. The published JSON Schema is gitignored and generated at build, so the `propertyNames` pattern lands there from the same constant. Right.
- Doors, read in the live tree: `defineStack` and `os validate` parse `objectExtensions` as `z.array(ObjectExtensionSchema)` (stack.zod.ts:821; cli validate.ts:317 reads `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`); the save, restore and draft-promotion doors and every sync that registers a stored row parse the body with `OBJECT_EXTENSION_ITEM_SCHEMA = z.preprocess(withoutProtectionEnvelope, ObjectExtensionSchema)` (protocol-object-extension-item.ts:75, :244; protocol.ts:2007 `registerStoredObjectExtension`). So every door that parses an extension refuses the key through the one schema; nothing is spelled twice. Right.
- Two readers never parsed and still do not: `ObjectQL.registerApp` (engine.ts:9446) copies `ext.fields` as given, and the marketplace install (marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1842, :3333) reads `body.objectExtensions` only for the `__c` judge and the patch-target judge, never through the schema. Both take an artifact `os build` already parsed, so a bad key reaches them only from a pre-upgrade artifact. The PR body names the fold; the changeset's door list also names "the marketplace install" among the doors that parse an extension, which it is not (see ② should-fix). The narrowing itself is consistent at every parse door.
- D3 detector `object-extension-field-key-grammar-refused`: predicate is the refusing door's own (`ObjectExtensionSchema.safeParse`, `invalid_key` issues at path length 2 under `fields`), through the shared `refusedExtensionRecordKeys(extension, slot)`, so it lists exactly the keys the parse refuses as keys and nothing else: a `__proto__` key is refused by the guard with a `custom` code and so is not listed, but that refusal predates this card and is not this narrowing's shape; a malformed field body fails with other codes and is not listed, correctly. It lists, never rewrites (`mapCollection` returns the entry), names the target, prints only the key and the field's `type` in `from`, closes each reason with the parse's message. Appended last in `REFUSED_STORED_SHAPES`, `toMajor: 18` = `PROTOCOL_MAJOR`, the id is the new semantic entry's id, the stored pass reaches `object_extension` rows through stored.ts:82. Right.
- Semantic entry 18: same shape as the sibling `object-extension-field-patch-key-grammar-refused` entry (id, surface, replacement, reason, acceptanceCriteria; no `relevantWhen`, as the sibling), filename derived from the id, no other file touched, no tracker number in the runtime strings. Right.
- Tests (read, not reviewed): refusal cases, controls, the 11-key agreement test guarded against vacuity, and the four detector pins including the no-crossing case between the two detectors; the ablation report says the five refusals, the agreement test and three listing pins go red when the key schema is reverted, with controls green.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29523-object-extension-field-key-grammar.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, the only published package the diff moves. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the PR body and the changeset, line-initial, one arm, matching: a value an author could write is now refused, so `narrowed`, BREAKING, at least `minor` on the moved package (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). The BREAKING banner, the FROM to TO line and the one-line fix are present. The ADR-0087 disposition is one marker, `adr-0087: registered object-extension-field-key-grammar-refused`, and that id is a new semantic entry in this diff, which is what `registered` requires. Skills-docs line present; `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx` gains the paragraph. The level and the declarations match the diff.

Should-fix (changeset prose, not the level): the "at every door that parses an object extension" list names "the marketplace install"; the install does not parse an extension with the schema (it judges `__c` and patch targets on the built artifact and hands the fold the body as given). Drop it from that list or say the install inherits `os build`'s parse, so the CHANGELOG does not promise a refusal the install door itself does not make.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Both out-of-scope findings in the report (the `registerApp` fold copies without parsing; `constructor`/`prototype` admitted on the extension) are the fold's trust model and a pre-existing sibling gap, correctly noted and not filed; neither is widened by this diff.
- Dev flags: none on the diff. `Premise-still-valid: true` holds against the tree: `fields` was `z.record(z.string(), FieldSchema)` at the merge base.
- Gate verdicts on `bd50ef25315a838988c2086cd5f2d6733bbc7b08` (REST, 15 readings one minute apart, 04:10:56Z to 04:25:17Z, and a last read at 04:25Z): check-runs total 0 on every reading; check-suites 5, all `queued` with no conclusion on every reading (objectstack-fleet, claude, vercel, fly-io, cloudflare-workers-and-pages); workflow runs for the head 0; combined status `pending`, 0 statuses. No gate has concluded on this head, no run is in progress, and none is claimed green: every derived gate family is still pending. The cause is on the board: the PR reads `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty`, and `git merge-tree origin/main bd50ef25` conflicts in `packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts` (the #29541 dashboard reserved-date-range detector landed on `main` at the same append site after this branch's merge of `87956dcc`). The pull-request workflows do not run on a head GitHub cannot merge. Escalated to the seat as a should-fix before the queue: re-merge `main`, keep both appended detectors and both ids in the `refused-shapes.test.ts` list, push, and let the gates run; the re-merged head needs its own record, since this one names `bd50ef25`.
- The report's local battery (spec 803/803, dispatch-gates 104/104, dogfood 402 passed) is the dev's reading, not a gate verdict, and is not adopted here.

### ④ Design judgment

- `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`: holds against its ruling (card #29523, the #29366 twin) and its first consumers. The one key constant now has three readers and its comment lists all three; the `fields` and `fieldPatches` records are spelled alike (`refuseRecordProtoKey(z.record(FieldNameKeySchema, X, { error }))`), so the two cannot drift. Tried to break it: a `__c` key in a vendor package or an unsuffixed key in a `.custom` pair still parses here and is refused by the doors' one `__c` judge (protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts), which the schema rightly does not re-spell; a key the target already declares is still the merge's and `refuseFieldPatchOfReplacedField`'s business; the root `superRefine` and `overwrite` (`materializeTreeSelfReferences`) still read `extension.fields` after the key parse and need no change; Studio's add-field derives its key through `toFieldNameLoose` and the `__c` suffix, so it writes a key the grammar admits. No must-fix.
- `packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts`: holds against the stored pass and the sibling detector. The shared helper filters on `slot`, so a row carrying a bad `fields` key and a bad `fieldPatches` key is listed once by each and never crossed (pinned). `from` prints `{ key: { type } }` only, so a field body with a default or help text is not echoed; a non-object field value yields `type: undefined` without throwing. The `fieldPatches` detector's `from` still prints the whole patch, a pre-existing asymmetry the diff does not widen. The detector's parse runs the whole extension twice when both slots are bad, which is a cost the stored preview can bear. No must-fix.
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-field-key-grammar-refused.ts`: holds against its first consumer, the detector of the same id and the upgrade guide. The surface names `objectExtensions[].fields` and the `defineObjectExtension` spelling; the replacement gives the snake_case key with the `.custom` suffix case; the acceptance criteria state the parse issue, the stored-row fate (the sync counts the row as an error and registers none of it, `fieldPatches` included; the next save is 422) and the `os migrate meta --stored` listing, each of which the code read above does. One prose point, no fix owed: the fieldPatches sibling says the sync "names the row (INVALID_METADATA)" where this one says "counts it as an error"; both describe `registerStoredObjectExtension` throwing into the caller's per-row handling. No must-fix.

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6923c61d2d2a3b3c145991a9d3ff30c11ff2e050 && git checkout 6923c61d2d2a3b3c145991a9d3ff30c11ff2e050
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2c91a55fc46c19979aba499fbdeea2022d784f35 649d47eabbc85188b8c8f9576dc7758266ed402e && git checkout -B drift-repro 2c91a55fc46c19979aba499fbdeea2022d784f35 && git merge --no-ff 649d47eabbc85188b8c8f9576dc7758266ed402e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2c91a55fc46c19979aba499fbdeea2022d784f35` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.
